method: Raw video is measured sample by sample: every pixel carries one luma sample and the chroma sampling adds one full colour sample per pixel for 4:4:4, one per two pixels for 4:2:2 and one per two pixels in both directions for 4:2:0, so the samples per pixel are 3, 2, 1.5 and 1 for monochrome. Bits per pixel is samples per pixel times bits per sample; the frame size in pixels times bits per pixel is the bits per frame, and multiplying by the frame rate gives the raw payload in bits per second. Dividing by eight and scaling gives bytes, with decimal storage units (1 GB = 10^9 bytes). The interface is the smallest nominal SMPTE payload rate (270 Mb/s SD-SDI, 1.485 Gb/s HD-SDI, 2.97 Gb/s 3G-SDI, 5.94 Gb/s 6G-SDI, 11.88 Gb/s 12G-SDI) that is at least the raw rate, and its utilisation is the ratio of the two. Blanking intervals, ancillary data, embedded audio and frame padding are not part of the count, so a real signal needs headroom above the bare payload figure.
